title: Quarto Listings
text:
Quarto Listings provide a way to organize and display collections of content on a website.
They are particularly useful for professional portfolios, blogs, and project galleries.


A Quarto Listing automatically generates a collection of pages based on files in a specified directory.
Listings can display information such as project titles, descriptions, dates, and categories.
This makes it easier for visitors to explore content without manually maintaining a long list of links.



Quarto uses YAML configuration to define which files should appear in a listing.
For example:
listing:
  contents: projects
  type: grid
  sort: "date desc"
This configuration tells Quarto to display content from a projects folder in a grid layout, with the newest entries appearing first.






Format
Purpose




Grid
Displays projects as visual cards


Table
Organizes content into rows and columns


Default
Displays a traditional list of entries






Quarto Listings could help me organize projects involving:

Digital marketing analytics
SQL and BigQuery
E-commerce and Shopify
Data visualization
Consumer behavior research

As I complete additional projects in the MSDM program, Listings can make my portfolio easier to maintain and navigate.



Learning Quarto Listings has helped me understand how websites can organize content dynamically.
Rather than manually adding new project links, I can use Quarto to automatically display new entries in a consistent format.

title: Customizing Quarto with CSS and SCSS
text:
CSS (Cascading Style Sheets) and SCSS (Sassy CSS) allow developers to customize the appearance of websites.
In Quarto, these tools help create professional, visually appealing websites that improve readability and user experience.


CSS controls how HTML elements appear on a webpage.
It can customize:

Colors and backgrounds
Fonts and text sizes
Spacing and alignment
Borders and layouts

For example, CSS can change the appearance of headings:
h1 {
  color: #2E86AB;
  font-weight: bold;
}



SCSS is an extension of CSS that provides additional features, including variables, nesting, and reusable styling rules.
For example:
$primary-color: #2E86AB;

h1 {
  color: $primary-color;
}
SCSS can make website styling easier to organize and maintain.






Feature
CSS
SCSS




Standard browser styling
Yes
Compiles to CSS


Variables
Yes
Yes


Nesting
Yes
Yes


Bootstrap integration
Limited
Strong


Quarto support
Yes
Yes






Quarto allows custom CSS files to be included through _quarto.yml.
For example:
format:
  html:
    theme: cosmo
    css: styles.css
This configuration tells Quarto to apply the styles defined in styles.css.



Quarto also supports SCSS files for customizing Bootstrap themes.
For example:
format:
  html:
    theme:
      - cosmo
      - custom.scss
This allows developers to customize Bootstrap variables and website components.



A well-designed website improves the user experience by making information easier to find and understand.
For a digital marketing portfolio, consistent colors, readable typography, and organized layouts help communicate professionalism.



Learning CSS and SCSS has helped me understand how website design connects to digital marketing.
Beyond making websites visually appealing, styling can improve usability, accessibility, and the presentation of analytical findings.

title: Home
text:
Tim Arana


Hello! I’m Tim Arana, a graduate student pursuing a Master of Science in Digital Marketing (MSDM) at California State Polytechnic University, Pomona.
This website showcases my academic experience, technical skills, and projects related to digital marketing, data analytics, and consumer behavior.


I am interested in understanding how businesses can use data, technology, and consumer insights to improve marketing strategies and customer experiences.
Through my graduate coursework, I have gained experience with marketing analytics, e-commerce platforms, SQL, and data visualization.
My goal is to continue developing my analytical and technical skills while pursuing opportunities in digital marketing and marketing analytics.



California State Polytechnic University, Pomona
Master of Science in Digital Marketing (MSDM)
Graduate Student




Marketing Analytics: Google Analytics 4 (GA4), Google BigQuery, SQL
Data Analysis: R, RStudio, Excel
Data Visualization: Tableau, Looker Studio
E-Commerce: Shopify, Google Merchant Center
Web Development: Quarto, HTML, CSS
Collaboration: GitHub, Microsoft Teams




My career goal is to work in digital marketing or marketing analytics, where I can combine data-driven decision-making with creative marketing strategies.
I am particularly interested in marketing technology, customer analytics, e-commerce, and the growing role of artificial intelligence in marketing.



I am currently working on a Culminating Experience Project involving CVRx and Salesforce adoption.
Our project explores opportunities to improve Salesforce engagement and adoption through data analysis and targeted recommendations.
My analytical objective focuses on Salesforce user segmentation and targeted engagement strategies.
